support_triage_agent.note: The support agent's one model call. Braintrust's own client wrapper writes no OpenTelemetry, so the capture script opens this span around the chat request and sets the braintrust.* fields Braintrust documents, as an application would. Its single score, correctness, is the case the conventions can hold.

scoring_span.note: No model call and no tokens: a grader's verdicts, which Braintrust records as a span of their own with type score. It carries three scores — correctness, helpfulness and tone — and the conventions hold one evaluation per span, so braintrust.scores is listed below as flattened rather than one score being picked.

RunnableSequence.workflow.note: The whole chain, prompt then model. LangChain emits no OpenTelemetry of its own; this span and the two beneath it come from Traceloop's LangChain instrumentation.

execute_task ChatPromptTemplate.note: The chain's first step: filling the prompt template with the question. No model is called on this span.

ChatOpenAI.chat.note: The chat request made by the chain's model step.

litellm_request.note: LiteLLM's record of the completion it routed: the model, what it cost, and its proxy's key and budget metadata.

raw_gen_ai_request.note: The request and response as the provider saw them, as llm.openai.* blobs beneath litellm_request. Nothing on this span identifies a library, so the translator leaves it alone; the facts it holds are read from litellm_request instead.

ChatCompletion.note: The chat request, recorded by OpenInference's OpenAI instrumentation.

support_triage_agent.workflow.note: Opened by @workflow(name="support_triage_agent") around the agent's function. It wraps the model call rather than being it: the call is its child span, openai.chat.

openai.chat.note: The chat request itself, recorded by OpenLLMetry's OpenAI instrumentation. It inherits the workflow's name as traceloop.workflow.name.

The chat request in the shape OpenLLMetry wrote before it adopted the conventions: numbered gen_ai.prompt.N.* attributes and gen_ai.system. Current releases no longer emit this, so it is written by hand.

POST.note: The HTTP request underneath the model call. It carries only http.* and server.* attributes, so there is nothing about the model here to translate.

chat gpt-4o-mini.note: OpenTelemetry's own OpenAI instrumentation, named the way the conventions say to: operation, then model. The control case — already written in the conventions, so the translator should find almost nothing to do.

call_model.note: A hand-rolled span with bare names like model and prompt_tokens, the way an in-house wrapper might write them. No library emits these, so it is written by hand.

call_model_sparse.note: One folk spelling and a token count under a name nothing reads. Two folk spellings used to be the minimum for the fallback to claim a span, so this one passed through untouched: a span manifestly reporting what a call spent, leaving with no record that the count had been walked past.

call_model_camel.note: The same exchange with promptTokens and completionTokens, the camelCase an in-house wrapper reaches for. The fallback claims the span on model and provider and reads neither count, so both are named in interlingua.lossy rather than mapped on the strength of a word.

call_model_packed.note: The whole usage object in one string, the shape LiteLLM's raw span carries. It is recognized and deliberately not parsed: lifting a number out of a Python repr by guessing at the shape is the silent mismapping the loss list exists to prevent.

GET /v1/chat/completions.note: The negative control. It carries a token word in a rate-limit header and a model name, and it is not a model call. Most spans in a pipeline look like this, so a detector that claims it has done more damage than the gap it closed: it must leave with no interlingua.* at all.

ai.generateText.note: The generateText call the application made: the outer span, in the AI SDK's own ai.* names. The agent's name, support_triage_agent, appears here as ai.telemetry.functionId rather than as a span name.

ai.generateText.doGenerate.note: The request to the provider, beneath generateText. It already uses gen_ai.* names, but spells the provider gen_ai.system.

ai.toolCall.note: The SDK running the lookup_order tool the model asked for. No model is called on this span.
